claims.text: The benchmark executes every support task five times to determine which outcomes persist.
An agent with a 0.60 success rate on individual attempts would theoretically achieve a 0.08 success rate across five independent trials.
The grading system evaluates performance based on final database state, adherence to policy, and the agent's actions, without using an LLM judge.
The policy evaluation consists of eleven specific functions that analyze the conversation trace.
The grading system does not mandate the use of an 'escalate_to_human' tool, even though the policy suggests it.
The testing backend is intentionally designed to allow the agent to attempt policy violations so that the system can observe whether the agent follows rules.
The 'pass^k' metric calculates the percentage of tasks that succeeded across all k trials.
When a simulated customer ends a conversation, the agent must receive a closing turn to prevent incomplete tool calls.
The initial run was abandoned after completing 60 of 75 trials because the daily token allowance was exhausted.
Policy violations were incorrectly logged because regex patterns failed to match specific customer phrasing regarding store credit and card refunds.
The system now requires a lookup for refusal tasks rather than mandating the use of an escalate_to_human tool.
If a run is terminated by a token cap, the system marks it as incomplete rather than assigning a score, as unfinished trials cannot be distinguished from failures.
The --regrade function allows for re-scoring finished trials from saved transcripts without incurring additional model costs.
The --dry-run command provides an estimate of the tokens required to complete remaining trials before execution.
A domain is defined as a directory containing three specific files.
The software package does not contain any hardcoded retail logic.
In a recent set of trials, 29 out of 37 state-changing operations occurred after the simulated customer had already exited the interaction.
Across 24 specific trials, every write operation took place after the simulated customer had departed.
The agent evaluation suite does not require the agent to generate any spoken output to successfully complete tasks.
All five trials for the unknown_email task were passed without the assistant speaking at all.
The twenty tasks included in the suite are manually created rather than being derived from actual support logs.
Five tasks were introduced to the suite after earlier testing revealed that nine out of twelve tasks had never experienced a failure across 88 trials.
The current suite does not evaluate how an agent handles an adversarial user attempting to force a refund.
The software is licensed under the MIT license.

Grading an AI agent without an LLM judge is possible by comparing final database states against expected outcomes.
Requiring an agent to call a specific tool can drastically change its success score, even if the agent otherwise behaves correctly.

Re-running AI evaluations to fix grading logic is a waste of resources when you can re-score existing transcripts instead.
If your evaluation harness doesn't distinguish between a failed trial and one cut off by a token limit, your final score is fundamentally dishonest.
